profiles.title: Downtown Tree Planters
description_lines: Raised concrete tree planters will increase tree canopy in the city's heavily urbanized
areas that have experienced significant tree loss over the years. Installation of one to
two tree planters/year, designed to provide needed protection for trees from plows,
cars and other common damages, while providing adequate soil and protection for
roots.

profiles.title: Victoria Park EV Charger
description_lines: A publicly available level 2 electric vehicle (EV) charger to be installed at a proposed
location near the batting cages. This will expand the City’s network of EV chargers
available to drivers of electric and hybrid vehicles.

profiles.title: Active Transportation (AT)
description_lines: Results to be achieved include:
1. Design and build of Local Street Bikeways in Parkdale and Sherwood (approx. 3km)
2. Design and engagement phases for Maple/Belvedere Ave
3. AT wayfinding project continuation
4. Design and engagement phase for Fitzroy St. or for AT projects in parkland
properties that will become key AT connections (e.g. Rosemount Park, East Royalty's
Montgomery Path, and similar)
5. Build essential, minor AT connections (e.g. trail-to-road transitions).

profiles.title: Public Transit Buses
description_lines: New buses will be purchased to replace aging transit fleet. In 2026-2027: four full-sized
buses to be delivered in the spring, six full-sized buses in December 2026 and two
battery-powered electric minibuses delivered in March 2027.

profiles.title: Transit Infrastructure
description_lines: To improve safety and accessibility, annual bus stop improvements such as concrete
pads, shelters, benches, poles and signs will be added. Technology investments are
being made to improve fare payment and automatic passenger counting systems, to
help modernize and improve the transit experience and reduce ridership barriers, while
providing needed data for transit management and planning.

profiles.title: New Fire Station
description_lines: Finalizing new fire station design, site and pre-construction.

profiles.title: Fire Engine Replacement
description_lines: Replacement of three fire engines over the next five years, starting with Engine 4 at
Station 2. These engines have exceeded their life expectancy as first response vehicles.
In accordance with fire service code and standards, front line vehicles are to be
replaced after 20 years of service. Replacing outdated vehicles will enhance firefighter
safety and operational capabilities required in our growing City.

profiles.title: New City Website
description_lines: The City’s charlottetown.ca website is an important platform for communicating with
residents and delivering public services. A total of $255,000 has been approved in the
2026/27 budget to support the development of a new municipal website. This
investment will enhance accessibility, strengthen transparency, and improve digital
service delivery for residents, businesses, and visitors. The redesigned website will offer
a more user-friendly experience, expanded functionality, and improved access to
important information and online services.

profiles.title: Multi-Use Outdoor Facility
description_lines: The outdoor sports facility located in the Elmer MacFadyen Memorial Recreational
Complex is at the end of its life; the city is unable to maintain the facility as an
aesthetically pleasing venue and to maintain safety standards.
A new outdoor facility will include a permanent artificial ice making system with a chiller
unit, new boards, lighting and playing surface. Ice-making has become challenging
due to changing weather conditions, and a permanent ice-making system will allow for
ice longer in the season, weather permitting. The City will engage with the public and
keep them up to date on the new and improved multi-use facility that will be functional
in all four seasons.

profiles.title: Simmons Artificial Turf Field
description_lines: Complete the design, drawings and cost estimate for a new artificial turf field that can
be used annually from April to November, accomodating up to 2,500 hours of use per
season. Construction is expected to begin in May 2026, with completion by the end of
July 2026.

profiles.title: East Royalty Landfill Old Road and
profiles.project: East Royalty Landfill Old Road and
description_lines: This work will enable the public to access the Parkman Soccer Complex, Acadian Forest
& Trails, East Royalty Park and the neighbourhood of East Royalty from Acadian Drive.
The scope of work includes resurfacing a large section of the old asphalt road,
constructing a gravel driveway for the remaining portion and constructing an Active
Transportation Pathway along the full length of the road and driveway.

profiles.title: Vehicle Equipment
description_lines: From bumper to bumper, police vehicles are uplifted with dozens of pieces of
equipment to secure and safely transport people, specialized equipment, technology
and seized property. These funds will support outfitting the new vehicles coming online
and replacement parts for existing vehicles.

profiles.title: Specialized Equipment
description_lines: Police officer equipment ranges from the everyday essentials to specialized tools, each
improving police outcomes. These tools carry the weight of justice, life and death.
Officers must be outfitted to provide first aid, collect evidence, interview persons of
interest, secure an area, subdue an assailant and more. Specialized equipment
includes tactical equipment, firearms, less lethal weapons such as CEWs, helmets and
goggles.

profiles.title: Communication Equipment
description_lines: Police officers rely on communication equipment to keep themselves and the
community safe. This equipment includes portable radios, car radios, speaker mics,
dispatch desk stations, charging stations and more.

profiles.title: Investigative Tools and Technology
description_lines: The department relies on various tools and technology to support crime prevention and
community safety efforts. As the community continues to grow, so to does the reliance
on technology. This capital investment includes the continued expansion of eWatch
and LPRs, BWCs, aerial support, surveillance equipment, digital forensic equipment and
forensic equipment. It also supports a system to centralize and operationalize the Real
Time Operations Centre.
The Community Camera program (eWatch and LPRS) supports crime prevention and
public safety efforts in real-time monitoring and investigation. These cameras provide a
valuable tool for deterring criminal activity by increasing the likelihood of detection and
prosecution. They also assist in gathering critical evidence, improving response times,
and ensuring accountability in both police operations and public interactions. Public
safety cameras enhance situational awareness, enabling officers to monitor high-traffic
or high-risk areas, such as entertainment districts, transportation hubs, and public
events, with greater precision.

profiles.title: Community Safety
description_lines: The department relies on field equipment to address its proactive and reactive policing
priorities. These funds will help complete the final fit out of equipment for the Incident
Command Post, address and support crisis/major incidents and events, and provide for
the continued investment in speed enforcement equipment (i.e., radar and lidar units) to
support our traffic enforcement capabilities and improve public safety.

profiles.title: Euston St. Redevelopment
description_lines: The building at 85 Euston Street is currently being redeveloped to become
Charlottetown’s new “Energy Innovation Hub”. The project is made possible by a
generous land donation from Irving Oil, as the property formerly operated as a popular
filling and service station for over 70 years. The structure was rebuilt in the 1930s by
Acadian architect Samuel Roy and is one of several similar stations built by Irving Oil
across the Maritimes. The building was designated a heritage property in 1997 and
remained in operation as a gas station until 2008.
The renewed facility, featuring level 3 electric vehicle (EV) charging stations available for
public use, will serve as a resource centre and collaboration space for advancing
climate action, contributing to the City and province’s targets of net-zero greenhouse
gas emissions by 2040 and net-zero energy by 2030.

profiles.title: Exhibition Drive Reconstruction
description_lines: A full street reconstruction is being undertaken on Exhibition Drive from Kensington
Road to Riverside Drive. This includes replacement of all underground infrastructure
including water, sewer, and storm water systems. A new 3-metre-wide asphalt
pathway is being constructed on the North side of the street.
This project will provide significant benefit to the community through improved
stormwater management, and improved capacity and reliability of utility infrastructure.
Additionally, this project will provide an important, safe, active transportation
connection from Kensington Road to Riverside Drive.

profiles.title: Pownal Street Parkade Upgrades
description_lines: The Pownal Street Parkade, a 465-vehicle parking garage located at 100 Pownal
Street, is currently undergoing concrete repairs and sprinkler system upgrades. This
facility was constructed in 1988, and while localized repairs have been carried out over
the years, the last major rehabilitation took place between 2008 and 2012. These
ongoing restoration projects aim to extend the service life of this facility.

profiles.title: Street Resurfacing
description_lines: This is an annual paving program focused on a worst-first approach while still giving
consideration to efficient coordination with other upcoming and anticipated projects.
At current costs, this reflects 4 per cent of inventory which is a 25-year return cycle.

profiles.title: Traffic Calming
description_lines: In an effort to ensure the safety of all road users, new traffic calming devices such as
asphalt speed humps and cushions, curb extensions, signage, etc. will be deployed at
key locations throughout the city. This project aims to reduce motor vehicle travel
speeds, and as a result, may also promote the adoption of alternative modes of
transportation by improving user comfort.

profiles.title: Sherwood Recreation Hall Upgrades
description_lines: The Sherwood Recreation Hall is slated to be replaced with a new community center
facility. A Masterplan for the area was undertaken as part of the City’s 2025-26 capital
budget. Funding will be allocated to the detailed design of the new facility, based on
the recommendations outlined by staff and external consultants.

profiles.title: North River Road & Capital Drive
description_lines: The intersection at North River Road and Capital Drive is one of the busiest
intersections in Charlottetown, and is a primary gateway into the city from communities
to the north and west. This intersection has experienced increasing demand over the
past number of years, which, at times, results in significant traffic delays and
congestion.
This project is aimed at increasing the efficiency of the operations of this intersection,
particularly for northbound traffic on North River Road during the afternoon peak time.
As part of this project, the North River Road leg of the intersection will be reconfigured
to have two dedicated left turning lanes, and one shared through and right turn lane. In
addition, the sidewalk in the immediate area will be replaced, and the intersection will
have asphalt resurfacing undertaken.

profiles.title: New Sidewalk Construction
description_lines: New sidewalk construction in the 2026/27 fiscal year includes new infill sidewalk and
paved paths in developed areas, totalling more than 3,700 metres.
